page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro architecture. Powered by 64-bit Arm Neoverse-V1 processor cores running at 2.6 GHz, this configuration provides 16 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume is bundled directly with the hardware, supplemented by an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include graphical processing units.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate exceptional throughput in the memory subsystem, highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3093.34 and strong large-block write memory bandwidth of 97.85 GB/sec. General compute benchmarks reflect median performance across the ecosystem, including a multi-core stress-ng result of 24505.16 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 13044.0. PassMark encryption testing falls in the lower quartile at 2224.38, and medium-scale LLM prompt evaluation exhibits reduced token processing rates.

The 8:1 memory-to-core density coupled with local NVMe solid-state storage makes the r7gd.4xlarge appropriate for memory-resident databases, real-time analytics, Redis deployments, and transactional caching systems. Because the included 950 GB NVMe disk provides ephemeral storage that does not persist across stopping the instance, data workflows must account for instance-store lifecycle constraints or integrate persistent network-attached storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r7gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by 16 dedicated 64-bit Arm Neoverse-V1 cores clocked at 2.6 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU profile, alongside an integrated 950 GB local NVMe SSD and an 8 Gbps baseline network connection. Benchmark profiles reveal high memory subsystem throughput, scoring 3093.34 in PassMark memory tests and delivering 97.85 GB/sec in large-block uncached write bandwidth. General computational performance aligns with median cloud benchmarks, though specialized cryptographic and machine learning prompt operations score lower. With its high memory allocation per core and low-latency local storage, the r7gd.4xlarge functions effectively for memory-heavy transactional databases, in-memory caching solutions, search indexes, and data processing pipelines requiring high read and write throughput.
